PANOORIN: Ayon kay Maria Bianca Perez, Head ng Quezon City Disaster Risk Reduction Office, nakaranas ng hindi pangkaraniwang lakas ng ulan ang lungsod nitong Sabado, Agosto 30, 2025, dahil sa localized thunderstorm.
Umabot sa 141 millimeters ng ulan ang bumuhos sa loob ng isang oras—mas marami pa kaysa sa ulang dala ng bagyong Ondoy noong 2009—na hindi kinaya ng drainage system.
Mahigit 36 barangays ang binaha at nagdulot ng matinding trapiko noong Sabado ng hapon.
Prayoridad ngayon ng lungsod ang pagpapatupad ng Drainage Masterplan, kabilang ang pagpapalawak ng mga drainage system upang makasabay sa urban development at mas matitinding pag-ulan. Posible ang pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto na sa usahay kusog nga mga pag-ulan. It is more precise as it utilizes Doppler radar technology to track real-time rainfall intensity, making it highly effective for immediate decision-making in flood-prone areas. A 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲, on the other hand, covers a 24-hour period but is issued only at the provincial level.  Stay inside if you are indoors – Don’t rush outside; protect yourself from falling objects first.
 Move to open spaces if outdoors – Keep away from buildings, trees, or power lines.
 After the quake – Check for injuries, hazards, or damage. Stay alert for aftershocks.
 Stay informed – Follow PHIVOLCS and trusted sources for official updates.

HAPPENING NOW | The Training Workshop on Climate Information Services (CIS) and Development of the ENSO Response Matrix Tool (ERMaT) is currently being held on September 2–4, 2025 at Citadines Amigo Iloilo. This 3-day capacity-building workshop brings together participants from DOST-PAGASA, DOST, LGUs, and partner agencies with the common goal of strengthening preparedness against the impacts of El Niño.
The workshop aims to introduce the ENSO Alert and Warning System and its role in early action planning, build awareness and technical capacity on climate information and services, and develop a sector-specific ENSO Response Matrix Tool (ERMaT) to support drought preparedness and climate risk management. It also seeks to foster collaboration among stakeholders for more coordinated and proactive responses.
As the sessions progress, participants are gaining knowledge on climate drivers, ENSO dynamics, and DOST-PAGASA tools, developing and calibrating local response matrices tailored to their sectors and communities, and strengthening networks for anticipatory action and climate risk management. Together, we are building resilience and safeguarding our communities against climate challenges.

DOST-PHIVOLCS kicked off the 5-day training on “Mainstreaming Disaster Risk Reduction into Local Development, Contingency Planning, and Emergency Preparedness through the Use of REDAS Software” for the Provinces of Dinagat Islands and Surigao del Norte. 
The training is being held at Southville Hotel and Convention Center, Butuan City on September 1–5, 2025. The program features three modules, including the use of REDAS for near-real time monitoring of earthquakes, tsunami and rain, for calculation of impacts, and for development of a community’s exposure database. 
Mr. Rosario JRA. R. Alon of Dinagat Islands PDRRMO and Mr. Cicero Cosme P. Tripoli, Head of Surigao del Norte PDRRMO, delivered the opening remarks. DOST-PHIVOLCS Director Teresito C. Bacolcol welcomed the participants and highlighted the importance of REDAS Training in empowering the local government amidst disasters and climate change. Ms. Divina Gracia B. Bandola, Programme Associate of the World Food Programme, also sent her message of support to this initiative. 
Participants from the Province of Dinagat Islands include representatives from the PDRRMO, Provincial Planning and Development Office (PPDO), Provincial Engineering Office (PEO), Provincial Architect’s Office (PAO), Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office (PENRO), and the Municipalities of Basilisa, San Jose, Tubajon, Cagdianao, Libjo, Dinagat, and Loreto. 
Meanwhile, participants from Surigao del Norte include representatives from the PDRRMO, PPDO, PEO, Sangguniang Panlalawigan, and the Municipality of San Isidro. Personnel from DPWH-Province of Dinagat Islands, DOST-Caraga, DILG-Caraga, DEPDev-Caraga, OCD-Caraga, Caraga State University, World Food Programme, as well as guest participants from Butuan City also joined.

Come and see these highlights! Participants can try the earthquake simulator to experience a simulated ground shaking.

देहरादून के इंदिरा नगर स्थित गौतम इंटरनेशनल स्कूल में बुधवार दोपहर अचानक आग लग गई, जब स्कूल में छात्र-छात्राएं मौजूद थे। तेज़ धुएं और आग की लपटों के बीच अफरातफरी मच गई। अग्निशमन दल मौके पर पहुंच चुका है और राहत कार्य जारी हैं। अभी तक किसी के हताहत होने की सूचना नहीं है।
यह घटना स्कूलों में अग्नि सुरक्षा उपायों की गंभीरता को उजागर करती है। समय रहते सभी बच्चों को सुरक्षित बाहर निकाल लिया गया, लेकिन यह एक चेतावनी है कि सुरक्षा उपायों की अनदेखी कितनी खतरनाक हो सकती है।
 *स्थान: इंदिरा नगर, देहरादून

READ | Fast lanes are now being implemented in hospitals to immediately cater to suspected Leptospirosis patients due to the rise in cases, according to the Department of Health Ilocos Center for Health Development (DOH Ilocos CHD) on Monday, September 1, 2025.  
Public and DOH hospitals, including Ilocos Sur Medical Center (ISMC) in this province and Ilocos Training and Regional Medical Center (ITRMC) in La Union, are required to set up these lanes, while private hospitals are encouraged to do so at their discretion.
As of  DOH Ilocos CHD’s  latest monitoring on August 16, 2025, 324 cases have been recorded in the region, a significant increase from 97 cases during the same period last year.  
Doctor Rheuel C. Bobis, head of the DOH Ilocos CHD’s Infectious Diseases Cluster, said the fast lanes guarantee that patients with symptoms receive priority treatment and have quicker access to medical attention.
“The incubation period of Leptospirosis can range from three to 14 days, but the typical incubation period is as early as five to seven days,” Bobis explained.
He added that this means symptoms could appear within that timeframe after exposure.  
Bobis stressed that the longer a patient waits for treatment, the higher the risk of life-threatening complications.  By Aila T. Villanueva

MAYON VOLCANO ADVISORY
06 September 2025
5:30 PM
This is a notice of increased seismic activity in Mayon Volcano.
Since 12:00 AM today, 6 September 2025, a total of 26 volcanic earthquakes have been recorded by the Mayon Volcano Network. RESCUE GROUP MOURNS LOSS OF FOSTER DOG ‘TIKTOK’
A local rescue group is mourning the loss of Tiktok, a dog who died in a tragic accident after slipping out while in foster care and being hit by a car.
Tiktok had been fostered to protect her from a distemper outbreak at the shelter. Rescuers said she was surrounded with love, but fate took a heartbreaking turn.
Once a victim of cruelty, Tiktok was previously shot five times with improvised arrows in Murcia, Negros Occidental. She was rescued by Bach Project PH on February 24, 2025, and made a full recovery.
A short viewing will be held on September 8, from 10 to 11 a.m. at Green Meadows Pet Aftercare in Negros, before her cremation. Attendance will be limited.
The group asks for understanding during this painful time and invites everyone to remember Tiktok with love and prayers.

[IN FRAME] | FCINSP JOEL A ELEFANTE, Acting Chief, Plans and Programs Division, FCINSP PAUL JORGE C BARROZO, Chief of the Logistics Division, FSINSP KENNEDY P TALINGTING, Chief of the Financial Management Division, and FO1 Michael P Bolaso, BAC Secretariat, participated in the 2-day seminar-workshop on the Project Procurement Management Plan (PPMP) for Calendar Year 2026.

Building resilience together: DOST-PAGASA, BPSU signs MoA for the Bataan Abucay Doppler Radar Station
08 September 2025 | The DOST-PAGASA and Bataan Peninsula State University (BPSU) formalizes partnership for the establishment of the Bataan Abucay Doppler radar station through a memorandum of agreement (MoA) signing held at the Amihan Conference Room, PAGASA Central Office, Quezon City. With the funding support from the Office of the President, through the Office of Civil Defense (OCD)/National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), the Bataan Abucay Doppler Radar Station will significantly enhance accuracy of weather forecasts through real-time data enabling local governments to issue timely warnings to communities, and plan disaster responses effectively.
DOST-PAGASA Administrator Dr. Nathaniel T. Servando welcomed BPSU officials led by University President Dr. Ruby Santos-Matibag, Campus Director Dr. Walter Valdez, and Dean of Instruction Dr. Dharell Siano. “Through this significant agreement between our institutions, we not only strenghten our shared commitment to nation-building but also foster collaboration in research, innovation, and capacity-building”, DOST-PAGASA Administrator Nathaniel T. Servando said. Dr. Servando’s appreciation is also extended to the OCD for closely collaborating with DOST-PAGASA in ensuring that lives and welfare of the Filipino people are safeguarded during natural disasters. 
Dr. Marcelino Q. Villafuerte II, Deputy Administrator for R&D, also expressed his gratitude to the BPSU for the establishment of the synoptic station in Abucay, Bataan in 2021, “with this signing ceremony, our partnership begins again and we hope that it could futher enhance our collaboration, as we establish our radar station, for students to potentially use our datasets.”
BPSU President Dr. Santos-Matibag highlighted that the signing ceremony is more than just a formal partnership, but a celebration of shared commitment to scientific process and public safety of all Filipinos. She also said that Bataeños are used to warnings pertaining to weather hazards, and this agreement highlights the university’s dedication to supporting research and innovation that address community needs, especially in DRR.
National Capital Region-PAGASA Regional Services Division (NCR-PRSD) Chief Engr. Lorenzo A. Moron thanked BPSU President Dr. Santos-Matibag and all involve, emphasizing that the ceremony today is more than technological advancement, but it also represents our promise to be better stewards of public safety. Other DOST-PAGASA Executive Staff members in attendance were Engr. Juanito Galang (Chief of Weather Division), Ms. Thelma Cinco (Chief of Climatology and Agrometeorology Division), Mr. Michael Bala (OIC of Research & Development and Training Division), and Mr. Oskar Cruz (OIC of HydroMeteorology Division). 
The PAGASA-BPSU Doppler radar station is expected to become a vital tool in strengthening the Philippines’ disaster preparedness, providing more accurate forecasts and timely warnings for the protection of communities across the nation.

Building resilience together: DOST-PAGASA, BPSU sign MoA for the Bataan Abucay Doppler Radar Station
08 September 2025 | The DOST-PAGASA and Bataan Peninsula State University (BPSU) formalizes partnership for the establishment of the Bataan Abucay Doppler radar station through a memorandum of agreement (MoA) signing held at the Amihan Conference Room, PAGASA Central Office, Quezon City. With the funding support from the Office of the President, through the Office of Civil Defense (OCD)/National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), the Bataan Abucay Doppler Radar Station will significantly enhance accuracy of weather forecasts through real-time data enabling local governments to issue timely warnings to communities, and plan disaster responses effectively.
DOST-PAGASA Administrator Dr. Nathaniel T. Servando welcomed BPSU officials led by University President Dr. Ruby Santos-Matibag, Campus Director Dr. Walter Valdez, and Dean of Instruction Dr. Dharell Siano. “Through this significant agreement between our institutions, we not only strenghten our shared commitment to nation-building but also foster collaboration in research, innovation, and capacity-building”, DOST-PAGASA Administrator Nathaniel T. Servando said. Dr. Servando’s appreciation is also extended to the OCD for closely collaborating with DOST-PAGASA in ensuring that lives and welfare of the Filipino people are safeguarded during natural disasters. 
Dr. Marcelino Q. Villafuerte II, Deputy Administrator for R&D, also expressed his gratitude to the BPSU for the establishment of the synoptic station in Abucay, Bataan in 2021, “with this signing ceremony, our partnership begins again and we hope that it could futher enhance our collaboration, as we establish our radar station, for students to potentially use our datasets.”
BPSU President Dr. Santos-Matibag highlighted that the signing ceremony is more than just a formal partnership, but a celebration of shared commitment to scientific process and public safety of all Filipinos. She also said that Bataeños are used to warnings pertaining to weather hazards, and this agreement highlights the university’s dedication to supporting research and innovation that address community needs, especially in DRR.
National Capital Region-PAGASA Regional Services Division (NCR-PRSD) Chief Engr. Lorenzo A. Moron thanked BPSU President Dr. Santos-Matibag and all involve, emphasizing that the ceremony today is more than technological advancement, but it also represents our promise to be better stewards of public safety. Other DOST-PAGASA Executive Staff members in attendance were Engr. Juanito Galang (Chief of Weather Division), Ms. Thelma Cinco (Chief of Climatology and Agrometeorology Division), Mr. Michael Bala (OIC of Research & Development and Training Division), and Mr. Oskar Cruz (OIC of HydroMeteorology Division). 
The PAGASA-BPSU Doppler radar station is expected to become a vital tool in strengthening the Philippines’ disaster preparedness, providing more accurate forecasts and timely warnings for the protection of communities across the nation.

SPMC AND BFP 11 SIGN MOA, JOINING FORCES FOR SAFER COMMUNITIES 
The Southern Philippines Medical Center (SPMC) and the Bureau of Fire Protection Region XI (BFP 11), headed by FCSUPT JUNITO F MASLANG, DSC, have officially sealed a partnership to strengthen emergency preparedness and ensure the health and safety of first responders.
Through a Memorandum of Agreement signed on 15 September 2025, both institutions committed to work hand in hand in addressing hazardous materials (HazMat), CBRNE events (Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Explosive), and other medical contingencies that threaten public safety.
Under the agreement, SPMC guarantees priority medical care for firefighters and BFP 11 personnel injured or taken ill in the line of duty. Both parties will also engage in joint training exercises and knowledge-sharing programs to boost readiness and enhance response efficiency.
In addition, a second Memorandum of Agreement provides that officers and personnel of BFP Region XI may avail of emergency, medical, and hospitalization services at SPMC which will be free of charge. These include burn treatments, minor surgical operations, post-admission treatments, and follow-up check-ups.
The ceremony was graced by leaders from both sides, underscoring the importance of this milestone collaboration. Representing BFP 11 were Regional Director FCSUPT JUNITO F MASLANG, Assistant Regional Director for Operations FSSUPT FRANKLIN O RATUNIL, Mindanao Team Lead FSSUPT RANDOLF V ARBUTANTE, and Davao City Fire District Fire Marshal FSUPT DONALD R CONCEPCION, along with other key officers. Representing SPMC were Legal Officer Atty. Karen Bianca Angeli S. Cezar, Medical Center Chief II Ricardo B. Audan, MD, and Dr. Fitzgerald C. Arancel.
This partnership stands as a testament to unity and preparedness, ensuring that our firefighters and first responders receive the care they deserve while safeguarding the greater community. September 19, 2025 - The Office of Civil Defense Region X (OCD X) conducted a site inspection in Valencia City, Bukidnon after a flash flood on September 17, 2025 that affected more than 2,000 families.
OCD X Regional Director and Northern Mindanao Regional Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NorMin RDRRMC) Chairperson Antonio B. Sugarol led the team in coordinating response operations and met with Mayor Amie G. Galario and City DRRM Officer June Ray A. Valero to assess urgent needs.
At the request of the Valencia City LGU, OCD X facilitated the augmentation of three (3) Water Search and Rescue (WASAR) Teams consisting of Special Operations Group of the Philippine Coast Guard, Northern Mindanao, the Cagayan de Oro City DRRMD (CDO-CDRRMD) WASAR Team and 4ID, PA WASAR Team.

TROPICAL CYCLONE BULLETIN NR. 11
Typhoon #NandoPH (RAGASA)
Issued at 11:00 AM, 20 September 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 5:00 PM today.
NANDO RAPIDLY INTENSIFIES INTO A TYPHOON.
Location of Center (10:00 AM):
The center of the eye of Typhoon NANDO was estimated based on all available data at 775 km East of Casiguran, Aurora (16.5_N, 129.4_E). 
Intensity:
Maximum sustained winds of 120 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 150 km/h, and central pressure of 985 hPa 
Present Movement:
West northwestward at 10 km/h 
Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds: 
Strong to typhoon-force winds extend outwards up to 500 km from the center 
TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNALS (TCWS) IN EFFECT
No Wind Signal currently hoisted.
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
Heavy Rainfall Outlook
Refer to Weather Advisory No. 3 issued at 11:00 AM today for the heavy rainfall outlook due to Tropical Cyclone NANDO and the Southwest Monsoon.
Severe Winds
NANDO will enhance the Southwest Monsoon as it approaches the landmass. Wind Signal No. 1 will be hoisted over Northern Luzon and the eastern portion of Central Luzon this afternoon, and the highest Wind Signal that may be hoisted throughout its passage is Wind Signal No. 5.
The Southwest Monsoon and the trough of NANDO will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):
_ Today (20 September): Bicol Region, Eastern Visayas, and Caraga
_ Tomorrow (21 September): Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Bicol Region, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Northern Mindanao, Caraga, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental.
_ Monday (22 September): Central Luzon (areas not under wind signal), Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Bicol Region, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Northern Mindanao, Zamboanga Peninsula, BARMM, SOCCSKSARGEN, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental.
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
Up to moderate to rough seas over the following coastal waters:
_ Up to 3.0 m: The eastern seaboards of Cagayan, Isabela, and Catanduanes.
_ Up to 2.5 m: The eastern seaboards of Batanes, Babuyan Islands, Polillo Islands, Albay, and Sorsogon; the remaining seaboards of mainland Cagayan; the northeastern seaboard of Aurora; the northern and eastern seaboards of Camarines Sur, Camarines Norte, and Northern Samar.
_ Mariners of motorbancas and similarly-sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
Coastal Inundation
There is a high risk of life-threatening storm surge with peak heights exceeding 3.0 m within the next 96 hours over the low-lying or exposed coastal localities of Batanes, Cagayan, Ilocos Norte, and Ilocos Sur. Refer to Storm Surge Warning No.1 issued at 8:00 AM today for the details
TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
_ NANDO is forecast to move generally northwestward in the next 12 hours before turning west northwestward towards Extreme Northern Luzon. On the forecast track, the center of NANDO may pass close or may make landfall over Batanes or Babuyan Islands between Monday (22 September) afternoon or evening. It may exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility by Tuesday (23 September) morning.
_ NANDO will continue to intensify while over the Philippine Sea. It may reach super typhoon category by Monday before its close approach to Batanes-Babuyan Islands.
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. Persons living in areas identified to be highly or very highly susceptible to these hazards are advised to follow evacuation and other instructions from local officials. For heavy rainfall warnings, thunderstorm/rainfall advisories, and other severe weather information specific to your area, please monitor products issued by your local PAGASA Regional Services Division.
The next tropical cyclone bulletin will be issued at 5:00 PM today.

Strong to typhoon-force winds extend outwards up to 580 km from the center

Wind threat: Strong winds

Batanes, Cagayan including Babuyan Islands, Isabela, Quirino, the northeastern portion of Nueva Vizcaya (Kasibu, Quezon, Diadi, Bagabag, Villaverde, Solano, Ambaguio, Bayombong, Bambang, Dupax del Norte), Apayao, Kalinga, Abra, Mountain Province, Ifugao, Ilocos Norte, the northern portion of Ilocos Sur (Sinait, Cabugao, San Juan, Magsingal, San Vicente, San Ildefonso, Santo Domingo, Bantay, Santa Catalina, City of Vigan, Santa, Caoayan), the northern and central portions of Aurora (Dilasag, Casiguran, Dinalungan, Dipaculao, Baler) and the northern and central portions of Catanduanes (Pandan, Caramoran, Bagamanoc, Panganiban, Viga, Gigmoto, San Miguel, Baras)
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
Heavy Rainfall Outlook
Refer to Weather Advisory No. 4 issued at 5:00 PM today for the heavy rainfall outlook due to Tropical Cyclone NANDO and the Southwest Monsoon.
Severe Winds
The wind signals warn the public of the general wind threat over an area due to the tropical cyclone. Local winds may be slightly stronger/enhanced in coastal and upland/mountainous areas exposed to winds. Winds are less strong in areas sheltered from the prevailing wind direction.
• Minimal to minor impacts from strong winds are possible within any of the areas under Wind Signal No. 1.
The highest Wind Signal that may be hoisted throughout the passage of NANDO is Wind Signal No. 5.
The Southwest Monsoon and the trough of NANDO will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):
• Today (20 September): Bicol Region, Eastern Visayas, and Caraga
• Tomorrow (21 September): Metro Manila, Central Luzon (areas not under wind signal), CALABARZON, Bicol Region, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Northern Mindanao, Caraga, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental.
• Monday (22 September): Central Luzon (areas not under wind signal), Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Bicol Region, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Northern Mindanao, Zamboanga Peninsula, BARMM, SOCCSKSARGEN, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental.
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
A Gale Warning is in effect over the northern and eastern seaboards of Northern Luzon. Refer to Gale Warning No. 1 issued at 5:00 PM today.
24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
Up to very rough seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 4.5 m: The seaboards of Batanes, Babuyan Islands, Cagayan, and Isabela
• Sea travel is risky for all types or tonnage of vessels. All mariners must remain in port or, if underway, seek shelter or safe harbor as soon as possible until winds and waves subside. 
Up to moderate to rough seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 3.0 m:  The northeastern seaboard of Aurora
• Up to 2.5 m:  The eastern seaboards of  Polillo Islands, Albay, and Sorsogon; the remaining eastern seaboard of Aurora; the northern and eastern seaboards of Camarines Sur, Camarines Norte, and Northern Samar
• Mariners of motorbancas and similarly-sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
Coastal Inundation
There is a high risk of life-threatening storm surge with peak heights exceeding 3.0 m within the next 72 hours over the low-lying or exposed coastal localities of Batanes, Cagayan including Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Norte, and Ilocos Sur. Refer to Storm Surge Warning No.2 issued at 2:00 PM today for the details.
TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
• NANDO is forecast to move generally northwestward in the next 12 hours before turning west northwestward towards Extreme Northern Luzon. On the forecast track, the center of NANDO may pass close or may make landfall over Batanes or Babuyan Islands between Monday (22 September) afternoon or evening. It may exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility by Tuesday (23 September) morning.
• NANDO will continue to intensify while over the Philippine Sea. It may reach super typhoon category by Monday before its close approach to Batanes-Babuyan Islands.

The program is part of the Holistic Weight Management and Health Promotion Program, which aims to encourage physical activity, improve blood circulation, and help prevent illnesses such as deep venous thrombosis (DVT), cardiovascular diseases, back pain, and arthritis.
During each session, all personnel participate in simultaneous stretching and movement to official accompanying music provided by the BFP, ensuring uniform implementation across all offices and fire stations in Region XI.
By diligently carrying out this initiative, BFP Region XI personnel not only strengthen their readiness to serve but also foster a culture of wellness, discipline, and unity within the bureau. 𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: The key difference between a 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 and a 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲 lies in their forecast period, coverage areas, and accuracy. 
A 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 provides forecasts for the next three hours and applies up to the municipal level. It is more precise as it utilizes Doppler radar technology to track real-time rainfall intensity, making it highly effective for immediate decision-making in flood-prone areas. A 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲, on the other hand, covers a 24-hour period but is issued only at the provincial level. It provides a broader outlook on potential weather disturbances but lacks the short-term accuracy of 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬.
For class suspensions or other official decisions, please refer to 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 issued by the respective PAGASA Regional Services Divisions.

The hybrid activity equips participants with the practical knowledge and skills to anticipate, prepare for, and respond to various natural hazards, from identifying risks to performing DRR measures as they continue to participate in a set of lectures and workshops in the coming days of the activity.

In line with 2025 Handa Pilipinas: Para sa Bagong Pilipinas – Mindanao Leg, DOST IX and DOST-PHIVOLCS co-organized a session on #MAGHANDA: Communicating Hazards, Risk, and Early Warning for Geologic Hazards last September 25, 2025, at Valencia Hall, Marcian Garden Hotel, Zamboanga City.
Participants from LGUs, the academe, and DRR practitioners in the Zamboanga Peninsula joined the forum, which featured lectures on geologic hazards, tsunami preparedness, hazard maps, and PHIVOLCS’ DRR tools like GeoRiskPH and REDAS.
DOST-PHIVOLCS Director Dr. Teresito C. Bacolcol reminded the participants that “preparedness takes resources, but inaction costs far more,” this event reinforces the call to use science-based tools and knowledge to protect lives and build resilient communities.

FORECAST:
Dinagat Islands and Surigao del Norte will experience rains with gusty winds due to Typhoon OPONG. Possible floods or landslides due to moderate to heavy rains to at times intense rains. Minimal to minor threat to life and property due to strong winds. Meanwhile Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao and the rest of Caraga will experience occasional rains due to the Southwest Monsoon. Possible flashfloods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. The rest of Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon (Habagat). Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Moderate to Strong winds from the southwest with moderate to rough seas (2.5 to 4.0 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang Dinagat Islands ug Surigao del Norte makasinati sa mga pag ulan ug kalit nga huros sa hangin tungod kang TY OPONG. Possible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto sa kusog ngadto sa usahay intense nga pag-ulan. Samtang ang Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao ug ubang dapit sa CARAGA makasinati sa katagkatag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagdalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili say uta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto sa usahay kusog nga pag-ulan. Ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto na sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Kasarangan ngadto sa Kusog nga hangin ang magagikan sa habagatang kasadpang direksyon ug kasarangan ngadto sa baluron nga kadagatan (2.5 to 4.0 meters).

PRESS RELEASE: MMDRRMC Preps for STS Opong, Regional Inter-Agency Coordination Cell Activated
According to PAGASA issued Tropical Cyclone Bulletin, at 5:00 PM today, OPONG maintains its strength while moving westward over the Philippine Sea. Metro Manila is still under Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal (TCWS) No. 1 and is expecting possible significant rainfall from Friday noon (26 September) until Saturday morning (27 September). Metro Manila might reach TCWS No. 2 or 3 at the most and overflow of nearby dams is not expected but not totally ruled out. 
Considering the recent weather update, the Metro Manila Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (MMDRRMC) convened for an Emergency Full Council Meeting attended by its member agencies and NCR Local DRRM Offices to discuss preparedness measures for the possible impact of STS Opong. The meeting was presided over by Chairperson Romando S. Artes and MMDA General Manager USEC Procopio G. Lipana, alongside Senior-Vice Chairperson and OCD NCR Regional Director George F. Keyser. The MMDRRMC Emergency Operations Center (EOC) and Response Clusters are activated and was followed by a special meeting for the activation of the Regional Inter-Agency Coordinating Cell (RIACC), headed by its Chairperson, Director Keyser. The DA RFOs in areas being affected by the Combined Effects of Southwest Monsoon enhanced by TC “OPONG” have undertaken the following:
1. Positioning of seeds for rice, corn and high value crops; drugs and biologics for livestock and poultry; fish stocks and paraphernalia on fisheries;
2.  Continuous coordination with concerned NGAs, LGUs and other DRRM-related offices on the impact of the weather systems, as well as available resources for interventions and assistance; and
3. Monitoring of prices and movement of agricultural commodities; and
4. Allocation of funds for insurance and credit by the Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation and Agricultural Credit Policy Council (ACPC), respectively.
AVAILABLE INTERVENTIONS
In response to the needs of farmers  and fisherfolk affected by the weather disturbances, the Department is ensuring that the following assistance are available:
1. Agricultural inputs (142,219 bags of palay seeds, 90,320 bags of corn seeds, and 40,518 kilograms of vegetable seeds);
2. 1,651,623 pieces tilapia, bangus and carp fingerlings;
3. Drugs and biologics for livestock and poultry;
4. Bags of rice stocks from the National Food Authority (NFA) for issuance to Local Government Units (LGUs) and other relief agencies;
5. Up to PhP 25,000 loanable amount from the Survival and Recovery (SURE) Loan Program of the Agricultural Credit Policy Council (ACPC), payable in three years at zero interest; and
6. Indemnification of insured affected farmers through the Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation (PCIC). 24 September 2025 – In line with the Bureau of Fire Protection’s (BFP) commitment to promoting health and wellness among its workforce, personnel of BFP Region XI, under the leadership of FCSUPT JUNITO F MASLANG, DSC, have been actively observing stand-up and wiggle exercises twice daily.
The program is part of the Holistic Weight Management and Health Promotion Program, which aims to encourage physical activity, improve blood circulation, and help prevent illnesses such as deep venous thrombosis (DVT), cardiovascular diseases, back pain, and arthritis.
During each session, all personnel participate in simultaneous stretching and movement to official accompanying music provided by the BFP, ensuring uniform implementation across all offices and fire stations in Region XI.
By diligently carrying out this initiative, BFP Region XI personnel not only strengthen their readiness to serve but also foster a culture of wellness, discipline, and unity within the bureau. SEEK SHELTER NOW! Severe Tropical Storm #OpongPH (BUALOI) is over MASBATE!
Severe Tropical Storm OPONG has slightly weakened but remains a dangerous threat as it traverses the Philippine archipelago. Expect powerful winds, heavy rainfall, and a high risk of life-threatening storm surge.
 TCWS No. 3 in Effect!
Storm-force winds (89-117 km/h) are expected in:
LUZON: Sorsogon, Masbate (including Ticao and Burias Islands), Albay, portions of Camarines Sur/Quezon/Laguna, Marinduque, Romblon, Oriental/Occidental Mindoro, and Batangas.
VISAYAS: Northern Samar, Biliran, and central portions of Eastern Samar, Samar, and Leyte.
Potential Impact: Moderate to significant threat to life and property.
 TCWS No. 2 in Effect!
Gale-force winds (62-88 km/h) expected over:
Metro Manila, the rest of Bicol, Cavite, Rizal, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, and more parts of Southern Luzon and Western Visayas.
Potential Impact: Minor to moderate threat to life and property.
Current Status (5:00 AM, 26 September 2025):
Location: Vicinity of Palanas, Masbate.
Max Winds: 110 km/h | Gustiness: 150 km/h
Movement: West Northwestward at 30 km/h.
 COASTAL HAZARDS: EXTREME RISK!
LIFE-THREATENING STORM SURGE with peak heights exceeding 3.0 meters is highly possible within 36 hours across low-lying coastal areas of Zambales, Bataan, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Mindoro provinces, Bicol Region, and most of Visayas.
Sea Travel is RISKY for ALL TYPES of vessels over the seaboards of Southern Luzon and Visayas due to very rough to very high seas. Mariners must remain in port!
 HEAVY RAINFALL & MONSOON (HABAGAT) ENHANCEMENT:
Refer to Weather Advisory No. 27 for the full rainfall outlook.
The Southwest Monsoon (Habagat), enhanced by Opong, will bring strong to gale-force gusts to areas not under a Wind Signal, including the Ilocos Region, CAR, Cagayan Valley, and Palawan today.
FORECAST: OPONG will continue moving West Northwestward across Masbate, Sibuyan Sea, Southern CALABARZON, and Northern MIMAROPA before exiting to the West Philippine Sea tonight/tomorrow morning.
ACTION ITEMS:
Monitor updates closely. The next bulletin is at 8:00 AM today.
Execute evacuation plans if you are in high-risk zones for storm surge or flooding.
Secure homes and belongings. Do not leave your safety to chance.

𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗗: Severe Tropical Storm (STS) Opong caused massive destruction as it battered large parts of the Visayas and Bicol Region, leaving at least four people dead and displacing more than 360,000 families, or about 1.414 million individuals, due to flooding and landslides.
In its 11:00 p.m. bulletin, PAGASA reported that STS Opong was located 260 kilometers west of Calapan City, Oriental Mindoro, as it moved over the West Philippine Sea. It is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) this morning or by midday, heading toward the northern part of Vietnam with sustained winds of 110 kph and gusts of up to 135 kph.
According to the Office of Civil Defense (OCD), more than 87,000 residents in the Bicol Region evacuated, while around 73,000 individuals remain in evacuation centers in Eastern Samar and Northern Samar.
In Masbate, three fatalities were reported, including one crushed by a fallen tree, while another person in Camarines Norte was struck by lightning. Around 20,000 people were affected in Masbate, governor Richard Kho said.
The storm impacted 11 regions, particularly 46 provinces, 391 cities and municipalities, and 2,891 barangays.
Experts have long warned that typhoons are becoming stronger and more frequent due to global warming, resulting in more severe damage to vulnerable communities.
STS Opong struck just days after Super Typhoon Ragasa, which killed at least nine people and displaced thousands in Northern Luzon. The back-to-back disasters have made it more difficult for local governments to provide aid and repair damaged infrastructure.
Meanwhile, as the public struggles with the devastation brought by successive storms, a major controversy surrounds government flood control projects. Investigations suggest that some officials may have profited from multi-billion peso kickbacks, allegedly spent on lavish lifestyles instead of urgently needed infrastructure against disasters. The issue sparked massive protests on September 21, 2025, at Rizal Park in Manila and at the EDSA People Power Monument in Quezon City.
The impact of STS Opong goes beyond the loss of lives and properties, it also highlights the deeper issues the country faces, from the effects of climate change to corruption in projects that should have served as vital defenses against natural calamities.

Kapag may baha, automatic na: “Kasalanan ng gobyerno!” Corrupt, palpak, walang pakialam. And to be fair, hindi mali. Ang laki talaga ng kasalanan nila. Ang daming budget na nilamon ng fake projects, ang daming drainage na ginawa para lang may masabing nagawa, tapos laging sira o bara agad. Ang gobyerno, dapat long-term solutions ang iniisip, hindi puro band-aid at photo ops tuwing baha season.
Pero let’s be real, hindi rin tayo malinis. Sino ba talaga ang nagtatapon ng basura sa kalye? Sino ang nagsisiksik ng plastic sa kanal? Sino ang nag-iiwan ng kalat sa ilog? Hindi naman si mayor o si congressman yun. Mga tao rin. Tayo rin.
So yes, the government failed us. Pero wag din natin i-deny, tayo rin may ambag sa problemang ‘to. Kahit gaano kaganda ang drainage na gawin nila, kung tayo pa rin mismo ang bumabara gamit ang sariling kalat, wala ring kwenta.
Truth hurts: Gobyerno + palpak na projects = baha. 
Citizens + walang disiplina = baha. 
Pinagsamang sablay? Guaranteed baha.
Kaya bago tayo magrereklamo, tanungin din natin ang mga sarili natin: "Am I part of the solution, or am I part of the problem?"
SA gobyerno, AYUSIN NYO TRABAHO NYO. SATING MGA CITIZENS, magtapon ng basura ng tama. Kung parehong palpak, wag na tayong magtaka kung lulubog tayo sa sarili nating kalokohan. WE ARE THE FLOOD. 
On a serious note, the government holds the biggest responsibility to protect the people, pero as citizens, may part din tayo. Kung sabay gumalaw ang gobyerno at ang tao, mas may chance pa tayo.

#EarthquakeAlert | Initial Report: Magnitude 4.6 Earthquake Hits West of General Nakar, Quezon
At 12:17 PM on May 27, 2025, a magnitude 4.6 earthquake struck west of General Nakar, Quezon. The quake, tectonic in origin and occurring at a shallow depth of 6 kilometers, caused light shaking that lasted approximately five seconds and was felt across several areas. 
These include parts of Metro Manila such as Mandaluyong, Marikina, Malabon, Pasig, Pasay, Pateros, Quezon City, Manila, and Makati; as well as areas in Cavite (Molino, Tagaytay), Rizal (Tanay), Laguna (Biñan, Cabuyao), Bulacan (Malolos), Pampanga (Angeles City), and Zambales (Cabangan). Authorities are monitoring for possible damages and aftershocks.

Vehicular movement remains completely halted.
Stranded commuters are being advised to remain patient and avoid risky detours.

Stay updated with official traffic and weather advisories before traveling.
Avoid movement through landslide-prone areas unless absolutely necessary.
Follow instructions issued by the local administration and traffic authorities.
Commuters are strongly advised to refrain from using the BTC Road until official clearance is announced to ensure safety.

Usa ka lalaking nag-jogging ang nakadiskubre sa patay'ng lawas sa babaye pasado alas 5 sa hapon, Lunes, Septyembre 29, 2025 sa Purok 3, Barangay Buenavista, Bansalan, Davao del Sur.
Sumala sa pagpanubay sa Bansalan Police, ang informant nagtug-an kanila nga samtang milabay siya sa dapit, nahibulong siya sa di maayong baho, rason nga iya kining gisubay sa pagtuong patay kini nga hayop. Apan taud-taod, nakuratan ang maong lalaki dihang nakita ang patay nga babaye nga wala'y sapot ug daling mireport sa kapulisan.
Atol sa pagsusi sa mga otoridad, gawas sa lawas sa maong babaye, napalgan sab nila ang mga sapot ug usa ka android cellphone.
Samtang giila ang biktima sa iyang higala nga si alyas Angel nga taga-Barangay Barayong, Magsaysay, Davao del Sur.
Gipalawman pa sa mga otoridad ang imbestigasyon sa insidente aron masuta kung kinsa ang mihimo sa krimen.

Ang tibuok Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto na sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Easterlies.  Aftershocks Expected – Residents are advised to stay alert and move away from damaged structures.
 Reported Impact – Several buildings and churches sustained cracks and partial collapses, roads were damaged, and power interruptions hit parts of Cebu and nearby areas.
 Casualties – At least 5 confirmed dead and multiple injuries reported in affected towns.
 Suspended Classes/Work – Local governments have suspended classes and government work today (Oct 1) for inspections.
Authorities urge the public to:
 Stay calm but vigilant
 Follow NDRRMC and PHIVOLCS official advisories
 Keep emergency kits ready

THE LOW PRESSURE AREA EAST OF SOUTHERN LUZON DEVELOPED INTO TROPICAL DEPRESSION “PAOLO”.
• Location of Center (7:00 AM):
The center of Tropical Depression PAOLO was estimated based on all available data at 760 km East of Virac, Catanduanes (14.1°N, 131.2°E).
• Intensity:
Maximum sustained winds of 45 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 55 km/h, and central pressure of 1004 hPa
• Present Movement:
Westward at 25 km/h
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds:
Strong winds extend outwards up to 360 km from the center
TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNALS (TCWS) IN EFFECT
 ➣ No Wind Signal currently hoisted.
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
 ➣ Heavy Rainfall Outlook
PAOLO is less likely to directly affect the weather condition of the country in the next 24 hours. Onset of heavy rains due PAOLO is possible by Friday (03 October) onwards. A weather advisory may be released today in anticipation of the heavy rains that PAOLO may bring over Northern Luzon and portions of Central Luzon.
 ➣ Severe Winds
Wind Signal No. 1 may be hoisted over the eastern sections of Northern and Central Luzon as early as this afternoon or evening. The highest Wind Signal that will likely be hoisted throughout its passage is Wind Signal No. 3. However, since the possibility of reaching typhoon category before landfall is not ruled out, the worst case scenario is Wind Signal No. 4.
 ➣ Coastal Inundation
There is a potential risk of coastal flooding due to storm surge in low-lying coastal areas of Northern and Central Luzon due to the passage of PAOLO. Storm surge warning may be issued today or tomorrow (02 October).
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
 ➣ 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
PAOLO may bring moderate to rough seas over the coastal waters of Northern and Central Luzon starting Friday (03 October) early morning. Gale Warning may be raised over the seaboards of Northern and Central Luzon as early as tomorrow (02 October) afternoon in anticipation of rough to very rough sea conditions. 
TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
• PAOLO is forecast to move generally west northwestward for the entire forecast period. The phenomenon of a red light in the sky during an earthquake is known as an earthquake light (EQL). 1. Piezoelectric Effect Rocks under extreme stress (from tectonic activity) may generate electric charges. When these charges reach the surface, they ionize air molecules, causing them to emit light (similar to auroras). 2. Friction Heating As tectonic plates slide past each other, friction can heat rocks to high temperatures, vaporizing minerals. These vaporized particles may glow red or orange when exposed to oxygen. 3. Charge Separation Stress on rocks can separate positive and negative charges. When these charges discharge into the atmosphere, they create plasma (ionized gas) that emits light. 4. Gas Emissions Earthquakes can release gases like methane or radon from the ground. These gases may ignite or react with air, producing red or orange flames or glows. EQLs are rare and vary in color (red, orange, blue, or white), shape, and duration. They typically appear before, during, or after an earthquake and are more commonly reported in regions with certain geological conditions (e.g., fault lines with quartz-rich rocks).

ICYMI: With the installation of the 96th Community Tsunami Alerting Station (CTAS) in Tandag City, Surigao del Sur, DOST-PHIVOLCS conducted the Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) campaign and Workshop on Tsunami Evacuation on October 2, 2025 at the Training Hall, CDRRMO Building/Operations Center, Awasian, Tandag City, Surigao del Sur.
The topics discussed were earthquake basics and tsunami generation, historical earthquakes and tsunami in the Philippines, introduction of REDAS earthquake and tsunami alerting module (REDAS-ETAM), PHIVOLCS Earthquake Intensity Scale (PEIS) as one of local tsunami Tsunami nature signs, Community-Based Early Warning System (CBEWS), 12 indicators for UNESCO Tsunami Ready Recognition Programme, and how to conduct tsunami drill. 
DOST-PHIVOLCS also held a Tsunami Evacuation workshop and developing Tsunami Evacuation maps--highlighting the importance for various communities to have a strategic tsunami evacuation plan which will guide residents in case a local tsunami will occur.

TROPICAL CYCLONE BULLETIN NR. 16
Severe Tropical Storm #PaoloPH (MATMO)
Issued at 8:00 PM, 03 October 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 11:00 PM today.
“PAOLO” MAINTAINS ITS STRENGTH WHILE MOVING WEST NORTHWESTWARD OVER THE WEST PHILIPPINE SEA.
Location of Center (7:00 PM):
The center of Severe Tropical Storm PAOLO was estimated based on all available data at 115 km West Northwest of Bacnotan, La Union (17.1°N, 119.4°E).
Intensity:
Maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 135 km/h, and central pressure of 990 hPa
Present Movement:
West northwestward at 35 km/h
Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds:
Strong to storm-force winds extend outwards up to 480 km from the center
TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNALS (TCWS) IN EFFECT
TCWS No. 3
Wind threat: Storm-force winds
Warning lead time: 18 hours
Range of wind speeds: 89 to 117 km/h (Beaufort 10 to 11)
Potential impacts of winds: Moderate to significant threat to life and property
Luzon:
The western portion of Ilocos Sur (San Vicente, Santa Catalina, City of Vigan, Caoayan, Santa, Narvacan, Santa Maria, San Esteban, Santiago, City of Candon, Santa Lucia, Santa Cruz, Tagudin) and the northwestern portion of La Union (Luna, Bangar, Balaoan, Bacnotan, San Juan, City of San Fernando)
TCWS No. 2
Wind threat: Gale-force winds
Warning lead time: 24 hours
Range of wind speeds: 62 to 88 km/h (Beaufort 8 to 9)
Potential impacts of winds: Minor to moderate threat to life and property
Luzon:
The southern portion of Ilocos Norte (Nueva Era, Badoc, Pinili, City of Batac, Paoay, Currimao, Banna, Laoag City, San Nicolas, Sarrat, Dingras, Solsona, Marcos, Bacarra, Piddig), the rest of Ilocos Sur, the rest of La Union, the northern portion of Pangasinan ( Basista, Lingayen, Villasis, City of Alaminos, Anda, Malasiqui, San Fabian, Mangaldan, Mapandan, Burgos, Dagupan City, Binalonan, Bolinao, Aguilar, San Manuel, Sual, Asingan, Labrador, Bani, Pozorrubio, City of Urdaneta, Laoac, Mabini, San Carlos City, Manaoag, Binmaley, San Jacinto, Bugallon, Infanta, Agno, Calasiao, Santa Barbara, Dasol, Sison, San Nicolas), Abra, the western portion of Kalinga (Tinglayan, Balbalan, Lubuagan, Pasil), the western portion of Mountain Province (Besao, Tadian, Sagada, Bauko, Sadanga, Bontoc, Sabangan), the western portion of Ifugao (Hungduan, Tinoc), Benguet, and the western portion of Nueva Vizcaya (Kayapa, Santa Fe)

Potential impacts of winds: Minimal to minor threat to life and property
Luzon:
The rest of Ilocos Norte, the rest of Pangasinan, Apayao, the rest of Kalinga, the rest of Mountain Province, the rest of Ifugao, the southern portion of Batanes (Mahatao, Uyugan, Basco, Ivana, Sabtang), mainland Cagayan including Babuyan Islands, Isabela, Quirino, the rest of Nueva Vizcaya, Zambales, Tarlac, Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, Bulacan, Aurora, and the northern portion of Quezon (General Nakar, Infanta) including Polillo Islands.
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
Heavy Rainfall Outlook
Refer to Weather Advisory No. 9 issued at 5:00 PM today for the heavy rainfall outlook due to Tropical Cyclone PAOLO.
Severe Winds
The wind signals warn the public of the general wind threat over an area due to the tropical cyclone. Local winds may be slightly stronger/enhanced in coastal and upland/mountainous areas exposed to winds. Winds are less strong in areas sheltered from the prevailing wind direction.
• Moderate to significant impacts from storm-force winds are possible within any of the areas under Wind Signal No 3.
• Minor to moderate impacts from gale-force winds are possible within any of the areas under Wind Signal No. 2.
• Minimal to minor impacts from strong winds are possible within any of the areas under Wind Signal No. 1.
Furthermore, the outer rain bands of PAOLO will also bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas not under Wind Signal (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):
• Today: Bataan, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Bicol Region, Panay Island, Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Northern Samar, and Eastern Samar
• Tomorrow (4 October): Batanes, Cagayan including Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Region, Zambales, and Bataan
Coastal Inundation
There is a minimal to moderate risk of storm surge with peak heights reaching 1.0 to 2.0 m within 12 hours over the low-lying or exposed coastal localities of Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Zambales, Cagayan, Isabela, and Aurora. Refer to Storm Surge Warning No. 10 issued at 8:00 PM today for the details.
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
Gale Warning is in effect over the seaboards of Northern Luzon and the eastern seaboard of Central Luzon. For more details, refer to Gale Warning No. 4 issued at 5:00 PM today.
24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
Up to very rough seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 6.0 m: The seaboard of Ilocos Sur
• Up to 5.0 m: The seaboar

Another student has developed a mapping website to help responders and donors locate earthquake-stricken communities in northern Cebu.
Charles Zoilo A. Yana, 21, a 4th year Computer Engineering student from Cebu Technological University Danao Campus launched the Northern Cebu Earthquake Relief Map Guide on October 2, 2025, just two days after the magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the province. 
The platform allows users to pin exact locations and share key details, enabling volunteers and relief groups to coordinate assistance more effectively.
Yana explained that the tool works similarly to Google Maps, though not fully precise, as it relies on free online tools and available application programming interfaces. 
He added that project is entirely self-funded and not school-related, but was built purely out of his initiative to assist affected families. 
"We have two options to pin locations: one is to search the place there could be, suggest and recommend dropdowns or just simply enter and it will try to locate the location," Yana explained.
"Second is manually, by clicking that green icon on the lower right corner, users can just zoom and navigate or find the nearest barangay," he added.
Since many affected residents in the north are offline and lack access to devices, Yana said the platform depends entirely on crowdsourcing from people with relatives or information about those in need. | via SunStar Cebu

Located in Sitio Looc, Brgy. Nailon, Bogo City, the team observed fault scarps, open cracks, and small pressure mounds within a 2-meter-wide deformation zone. Initial field mapping recorded about 200 meters of surface rupture, while drone surveys revealed the fault may extend up to 1.5 kilometers, showing signs of right-lateral movement. Field verification is ongoing to determine the full extent of the rupture.

BAGYONG “PAOLO” MAGDADALA NG MALAKAS NA ULAN SA NUEVA VIZCAYA AT KALAPIT-LUGAR
Nagbabala ang PAGASA na asahan ang matinding pagbuhos ng ulan sa malaking bahagi ng Hilagang Luzon dala ng Severe Tropical Storm “Paolo”. Ayon sa Weather Advisory No. 6 na inilabas nitong Oktubre 2, 2025 alas-11 ng gabi, posibleng umabot sa 100 hanggang 200 milimetro ang ulan bukas hanggang gabi sa Nueva Vizcaya, kasama ang Cagayan, Kalinga, Mountain Province, Ifugao, Benguet, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan at Nueva Ecija. Mas malakas pa ang inaasahang ulan sa Isabela, Quirino at Aurora na maaaring lumampas sa 200 milimetro. Binalaan ng mga eksperto na mas mataas pa ang epekto sa mga kabundukan at matataas na lugar, na posibleng magdulot ng landslide at pagbaha.
Mula bukas ng gabi hanggang Sabado ng gabi, Oktubre 4, patuloy pa rin ang malalakas na ulan sa Ilocos Region, Benguet, Abra, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Zambales at Tarlac. Dahil dito, mahigpit na pinapayuhan ang mga residente at mga lokal na pamahalaan na magsagawa ng agarang paghahanda at sumunod sa mga abiso ng kani-kanilang DRRMO. Ipinaliwanag din ng PAGASA na ang Weather Advisory ay nagbibigay ng mas malawak na tanaw sa loob ng 24 oras, habang ang Heavy Rainfall Warning ay nakatuon sa susunod na tatlong oras gamit ang Doppler radar na mas eksakto para sa mga agarang desisyon tulad ng class suspensions at paglilikas. Ang susunod na abiso ay ilalabas bukas ng alas-5 ng umaga.

Issued at 9:00AM, 04 October 2025 Hydrological Situationer #30 for Agno River Issued at 9:00AM, 04 October 2025 Paano mabubuo Ang bagyo ay nabubuo sa ibabaw ng karagatan kung saan ang temperatura ng tubig ay mataas at mayroong kahalumigmigan sa hangin. Narito ang mga hakbang sa pagbuo ng bagyo: Pagsingaw ng Tubig*: Ang araw ay nagpapainit sa tubig ng karagatan, na nagreresulta sa pagsingaw ng tubig patungo sa atmospera. *Pagtaas ng Hangin*: Ang mainit na hangin na mayroong kahalumigmigan ay tumataas patungo sa mataas na altitude. *Pagkondensa ng Ulap*: Sa pagtaas ng hangin, ito ay lumalamig at nagiging sanhi ng pagkondensa ng singaw ng tubig sa anyo ng mga ulap. *Pagbuo ng Low-Pressure Area*: Ang pagtaas ng hangin at pagkondensa ng ulap ay lumilikha ng isang lugar na may mababang presyon sa ibabaw ng karagatan. *Pag-ikot ng Hangin*: Ang hangin mula sa paligid ay dumadaloy patungo sa gitna ng low-pressure area, na nagiging sanhi ng pag-ikot ng hangin dahil sa epekto ng Coriolis. *Paglakas ng Bagyo*: Kung ang mga kondisyon ay angkop (sapat na init ng tubig at kahalumigmigan), ang sistema ay patuloy na lumalakas at nagiging isang bagyo. *Pag-uuri ng Bagyo*: Depende sa lakas ng hangin at organisasyon ng sistema, ito ay maaaring uriin bilang tropical depression, tropical storm, o typhoon kung ito ay lumakas pa. Ang mga bagyo ay karaniwang nabubuo sa mga rehiyon na malapit sa ekwador, kung saan ang temperatura ng tubig ay sapat na mainit upang suportahan ang pagbuo ng mga bagyo.

Cebu Provincial Government healthcare consultant Elisse Catalan has reminded motorists and volunteers to avoid congesting roads in northern Cebu as relief operations continue for communities affected by the magnitude 6.9 earthquake.
In a public statement on Saturday, October 4, 2025, Catalan said the increasing number of private vehicles heading north to deliver relief goods has caused heavy traffic, hindering the movement of ambulances, medical teams, and other essential deliveries such as water tankers and generators.
She added that vehicular accidents were already reported on Friday, which could further worsen the situation and delay emergency responses.
“Help is always welcome. Many want to do something to ease the helplessness or frustration with the pace of distribution. But care should go beyond providing relief,” Catalan said. 
“Response and rehabilitation after the earthquake will go beyond this weekend. The road ahead is long, and we will need sustained support,” she added.

Strong to storm-force winds extend outwards up to 430 km from the center

No Wind Signal currently hoisted.
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
Severe Winds
The outer rain bands of PAOLO will also bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):
• Today: Batanes, northern portion of mainland Cagayan including Babuyan Islands, Apayao, Zambales, and Bataan.
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
Up to moderate to rough seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 3.0 m: The seaboard of Ilocos Region.
• Up to 2.5 m: The seaboards of Batanes, Babuyan Islands, and Zambales.
• Up to 2.0 m:  The seaboards of mainland Cagayan, Isabela, and Bataan.

National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) Chair and Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. issued several directives to national and regional government agencies in response to the magnitude 6.9 earthquake that hit Cebu on Tuesday evening.
In a coordination meeting held on Wednesday, October 1, at the Government Command and Control Center (GCCC) Visayas hub in Cebu, Sec. Teodoro met with members of the Central Visayas Regional DRRMC. Among key directives were immediate assessment for response planning; efficient logistics management; close coordination with local government units (LGUs) to address priority needs, including access to potable water; augmentation of response personnel and teams; and establishment of additional coordination hubs in affected areas.
The Secretary continues to lead the National Inter-Agency Coordinating Cell (NIACC), overseeing response operations for both the earthquake and the impacts of recent Tropical Cyclones "Opong" and "Nando."
The series of meetings aimed to ensure that affected communities receive immediate assistance and that inter-agency support remains coordinated, responsive, and efficient. | via Civil Defense PH

BREAKING: The Commission on Elections (COMELEC) En Banc issued a Certificate of Finality on October 1 affirming the executory cancellation of the Duterte Youth party-list’s registration for the 20th Congress due to non-compliance with the requirements for publication and hearing. 
Additional grounds for the cancellation of the party registration include false representation of the youth sector and untruthful statements about its nominees. 
Despite the Duterte Youth filing a petition for a temporary restraining order (TRO) with the Supreme Court on September 3, the final decision was rendered after the lapse of the 30-day period without the issuance of a TRO.
COMELEC further noted that the Duterte Youth's mass withdrawal, substitution, and repeated switching of nominees during the 2019 elections undermined the intent of the party-list system and constituted a mockery of the electoral process.
On October 2, three winning party-lists are proclaimed to fill the congressional seats in the House of Representatives vacated by the Duterte Youth, namely Abono Party-list, Murang Kuryente Party-list, and Ang Probinsyano Party-list.

Bone chambers and tombs were destroyed at the New Corazon Cemetery in Barangay Sambag, Bogo City, following the magnitude 6.9 earthquake that struck Cebu province last September 30.

Metro Manila and Cebu City, Philippines — The Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Mines and Geosciences Bureau (DENR-MGB) has deployed an eight-member team of geologists, consisting of six from the Central Office and two from Regional Office VII, to conduct a comprehensive Post-Disaster Geohazards Assessment across several areas in Cebu Province. The assessment aims to identify zones susceptible to flooding, rain-induced landslides, ground subsidence, and sinkhole formation.
The initiative aims to enhance public safety and guide local government units (LGUs) in land-use planning and disaster risk reduction, particularly in communities situated on karst terrains characterized by limestone formations that are prone to dissolution and collapse.
According to Assistant Secretary for Mining Concerns and concurrent OIC Director Engr. Michael V. Cabalda, the assessment involves ground validation and geohazards data analysis. “This study will enable us to pinpoint areas susceptible to flooding, rain-induced landslides, and those areas with high potential for ground subsidence and provide technical recommendations to LGUs for proper zoning, building regulation, and emergency preparedness,” the Engr. Cabalda said.

Liquefaction is a phenomenon where a solid or a gas transforms into a liquid state. Let's explore it in different contexts relevant to the Philippines. *What is Liquefaction?* Liquefaction occurs when a solid material, often soil or sand saturated with water, loses its strength and stiffness due to increased pore water pressure, typically caused by seismic shaking during earthquakes. This leads the solid to behave like a liquid. *Causes of Liquefaction* 1. *Earthquakes*: Ground shaking can cause water-saturated granular soils (like sand) to lose strength. 2. *Water Saturation*: Soils that are fully saturated with water are more prone to liquefaction. 3. *Soil Composition*: Loose, granular soils are more susceptible. *Effects of Liquefaction* - *Structural Damage*: Buildings and infrastructure can suffer significant damage or collapse. - *Ground Settlement*: Areas can experience uneven settling. - *Lateral Spreading*: Ground can move laterally, damaging structures. *Liquefaction in the Philippines* The Philippines is seismically active, located in the Pacific Ring of Fire, making it vulnerable to earthquakes and associated hazards like liquefaction. Areas with soft, water-saturated soils are at higher risk. *Notable Examples* - *1990 Luzon Earthquake*: Caused significant damage, illustrating the country's vulnerability to seismic hazards. - *Areas at Risk*: Regions like Metro Manila, parts of Luzon, and other seismically active zones could be susceptible depending on soil conditions. *Mitigation and Considerations* - *Geotechnical Investigations*: Assessing soil conditions is crucial for construction in prone areas. - *Engineering Designs*: Structures can be designed to mitigate liquefaction risks. - *Land Use Planning*: Awareness and planning can help reduce risks. *Other Contexts* Liquefaction can also refer to processes in industries (like LNG - Liquefied Natural Gas) or natural processes like mudflows, but earthquake-induced soil liquefaction is often a key concern in seismic zones like the Philippines. Around 134 Pangasinenses gathered on Thursday, October 2, at the Lay Formation Center in Dagupan City for Rappler’s #MakePangasinanLiveable public forum. 
Local officials, community leaders, and citizens came together to talk about urgent concerns in the community, including flooding, education, healthcare, public safety, and good governance, and what can be done together to address them.
The public forum is part of Rappler’s civic empowerment roadshow, “#AmbagNatin: Engage for Change,” which aims to bring people and institutions together to shape better communities from the ground up.
This Pangasinan leg was organized in partnership with the Archdiocese of Lingayen-Dagupan and the AB English Language program of Pangasinan State University Lingayen Campus, with food sponsorship by Mang Inasal.

DISASTER RESPONSE UPDATE | 𝐁𝐎𝐂 𝐄𝐱𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐀𝐢𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐄𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐡𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐤𝐞-𝐇𝐢𝐭 𝐅𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐂𝐞𝐛𝐮
To help the victims of the recent earthquake in Cebu, the Bureau of Customs (BOC) turned over abandoned and forfeited goods to the Office of Civil Defense (OCD).
The donation, which came mostly from the Manila International Container Port (MICP), includes 56 pieces of Rapid Emergency Tents and 1,087 pieces of assorted tents to serve as temporary shelters, 50 units of mobile power supply to provide electricity in affected areas, and one bio-toilet unit to ensure proper sanitation for displaced residents. 
The donated items were declared abandoned and subsequently forfeited in favor of the government. In line with customs procedures and upon approval, these goods were officially released and turned over to the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) to support its ongoing relief and recovery efforts.
Aside from the forfeited items, BOC officials and personnel also donated over 100 sacks of rice to support food assistance efforts.
BOC Commissioner Ariel F. Nepomuceno, who previously served as Undersecretary of the Department of National Defense and Administrator of the OCD, emphasized the significance of ensuring that government resources are directed to the people in times of crisis. 
“In moments like this, every donation can make a difference for our countrymen who have lost their homes and security. Having worked with the OCD in the past, alam ko po firsthand kung gaano kahalaga na mabilis, maayos, at diretso ang tulong sa mga kababayan nating nasalanta," said Commissioner Nepomuceno.
MICP District Collector Rizalino Jose C. Torralba expressed his full support for the initiative, reaffirming the Port’s commitment to utilizing abandoned and forfeited goods for the benefit of the public.
“The Manila International Container Port stands in full support of the BOC’s thrust to transform abandoned goods into opportunities for service. Through this donation, we hope to extend help and bring comfort to our fellow Filipinos in Cebu who are recovering from this calamity,” said Collector Torralba.
The OCD will handle the distribution of the donated items to affected families in Cebu, ensuring that they reach communities most in need. This partnership highlights the coordination of government agencies to maximize resources and deliver timely support during emergencies.
Source: Bureau of Customs PH

Cebu’s Fault Line: What You Need to Know
Cebu is not just a busy and modern city, it also sits on top of the Central Cebu Fault System, a major fault line that can generate strong earthquakes.
This fault runs through Danao, Compostela, Cebu City, Talisay, Minglanilla, Naga, Balamban, and Toledo. It has four main faults: Balamban, Central Highland, Uling-Masaba, and Lutac-Jaclupan. The longest, the Uling-Masaba Fault, can produce a magnitude 7.1 quake, as strong as the 2013 Bohol earthquake.
Cebu has already felt strong earthquakes before, including the 2012 Negros quake, the 2013 Bohol quake, and the 2025 Cebu quake. These remind us that the risk is real.
This isn’t to cause fear, but to raise awareness. Earthquakes cannot be prevented, but being prepared, through stronger buildings, disaster drills, and emergency kits, can save lives.
Stay informed. Stay prepared.

Walk-the-Fault sa Davao City, sinimulan na!
Bilang panimula ng 2025 Walk-the-Fault activity sa Davao City, isang simultaneous Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) campaign ang isinagawa sa mga barangay ng Lacson, Wangan, Mintal, Balengaeng, at Bago Oshiro. Katuwang ang DOST XI, OCD XI, Davao City Government, Davao City DRRMO, at mga Brgy. DRRM Committee, nagbigay ang DOST-PHIVOLCS ng lecture tungkol sa panganib ng active fault at lindol.
Kasunod nito ay ang walk-the-fault at paglalagay ng markers sa mga lugar na dinadaanan ng Central Davao Fault System - Dacudao Segment sa Brgy. Mintal. Ito ay sa pangunguna ni DOST-PHIVOLCS Senior Science Research Specialist (SRS) Kathleen Papiona, OCD XI Director Ednar Dayanghirang, DOST XI- PSTO SRS Eric Miyones, at Davao City DRRMO Head PLTCOL Alfredo Baloran (Ret.). 
Layunin ng aktibidad na ipaalam ang active faults sa lugar upang maiwasan ang pagtatayo ng anumang gusali sa ibabaw nito. Itinuturo rin ang iba't ibang panganib ng lindol sa komunidad upang maibsan o mabawasan ang epekto ng isang malakas ng lindol.

Twelve student journalists and communicators from Pangasinan joined Rappler’s three-day training on journalism for community building, held from September 29 to October 1, at the Pangasinan State University Lingayen Campus.
These local storytellers will serve as civic engagement volunteers, known as Movers, and will form Rappler’s pioneering volunteers hub in Pangasinan. 
They covered Rappler’s public forum with community leaders and Pangasinan officials on Thursday, October 2. 
These activities are part of Rappler’s civic empowerment roadshow “#AmbagNatin: Engage for Change,” in partnership with Pangasinan State University (AB English Program – Lingayen Campus) and the Archdiocese of Lingayen-Dagupan. This was also sponsored by Mang Inasal Philippines.

As rains continue to flood parts of the country, health experts are sounding the alarm on leptospirosis — a serious infection that can be life-threatening if not treated early.
The Pediatric Nephrology Society of the Philippines, a group of local kidney specialists for kids, recently shared tips on how to spot and prevent leptospirosis, especially in children.
What is leptospirosis?
It’s a disease you can get by:
 Wading in floodwater
 Drinking water contaminated with rat urine or waste from other infected animals
 The bacteria (called leptospira) can enter your body through:
Open wounds
Scratches or broken skin soaked in floodwater
 Symptoms to watch out for:
Fever
Headache
Stomach pain
Red eyes
Yellowing of the skin (jaundice)
Trouble peeing
Shortness of breath
 Preventive meds you should know about:
If your child has waded through floodwater even just once, here’s what the experts recommend:
 Doxycycline 100 mg (2 tablets within 24 hours) — available for free at health centers
 Azithromycin (10 mg/kg single dose, max 500 mg)
 Amoxicillin (50 mg/kg/day, every 6 hours for 3–5 days, max 500 mg per dose)
If exposure happened over 7 days ago, they should take medicine again after a week.
OpinYonistas, avoid floodwater if you can.

Climate campaigners led by the Asian Peoples’ Movement on Debt and Development (APMDD) hold a protest outside a hotel in Pasay City on Tuesday, October 7, 2025, as the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) Board meets. 
“In the Philippines and throughout Asia, climate disasters have resulted in massive losses of livelihoods, infrastructure, crops, and even lives. Both economic and non-economic losses are increasing dramatically with each passing year, but governments of the Global North are not meeting their responsibility to mobilize adequate resources,” said climate activist and APMDD coordinator Lidy Nacpil.  
“They are extremely reluctant to provide the funds they owe to the South. Climate impacts are estimated to cost at least $894 billion annually by 2030, a conservative figure that doesn’t account for lost lives, cultures, and ecosystems. In truth, rich countries should be paying a total of at least $1 trillion per year to the FRLD. Yet governments have delivered only $360 million, which is nowhere near enough," she added.
The group called on Global North governments to increase funding for climate loss and damage and to stop financing what they described as the Gaza genocide. Headquarters Naval Forces Central (HNFC), Naval Base Rafael Ramos (NBRR), Lapu-Lapu City, October 7, 2025 – The arrival of BRP DAGUPAN CITY (LS551) at Maya Port, Daanbantayan on October 6, 2025 marked a significant boost in the ongoing relief and rehabilitation efforts in Northern Cebu. The PN ship delivered essential relief supplies and heavy equipment to support communities severely affected by the recent earthquake, underscoring the Philippine Navy’s vital role in accelerating recovery operations in the Visayas region.
LS551 brought a substantial shipment of relief aid, food packs, clean drinking water, hygiene kits, medical supplies and temporary shelters, providing essential support to communities struggling in the wake of the disaster. Beyond basic necessities, the PN ship also carried vital support equipment to enhance on-ground coordination. Among its cargoes were the vehicles from Valenzuela Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (VDRRMO) as well as the Communications Van from Naval Cyber Warfare Force (NCWF). Relatedly, said Communications Van will serve as a platform to provide mobile, reliable and secure communication support to naval and joint operations especially to the two (2) PN Disaster Response and Rescue Teams (DRRT) of this Command that were deployed to Joint Task Force “HANDA” under the Visayas Command to address the concern of some areas in Northern Cebu where fixed communication infrastructure is unavailable, damaged or disrupted. 
COMMO JOSELITO E DE GUZMAN PN, Commander, Naval Forces Central (CNFC) personally supervised the overall conduct of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Response (HADR) operations carried out by Team NFC in Northern Cebu, particularly in the Municipalities of Daanbantayan, Bantayan Island, and Medellin. His leadership ensured the synchronized execution of relief distribution, logistics coordination and inter-agency collaboration with the Office of Civil Defense 7 (OCD7), Department of Social Welfare and Development 7 (DSWD7) and concerned Local Government Units (LGU). Through his direct supervision, the Command was able to maximize the efficiency of maritime and land-based operations, guarantee the timely delivery of essential aid, and uphold the Navy’s commitment in serving communities affected by the recent calamity.
Following the relief mission in Daanbantayan, LS551 proceeded to Cebu via Capt Veloso Pier, NBRR to offload remaining essential supplies in support to ongoing HADR operations. The ship will then accommodate new load of relief goods and rehabilitation materials bound for the hardest-hit areas in Northern Cebu, further bolstering relief, recovery and rebuilding efforts. While currently docked in Cebu, LS551 remains on standby and ready to accommodate both rolling and loose cargos intended for continued relief and rehabilitation efforts in the affected Northern Cebu communities.
Naval Forces Central, Your Navy in the Visayas remains steadfast in its commitment in delivering swift and efficient disaster response. With the continued deployment of assets like LS551, NFC ensures timely support for both relief and rehabilitation efforts, working hand-in-hand with local and national agencies to restore communities affected by calamities.

Ang pangunahing dahilan ay ang korapsyon. Ang mga opisyal at kontraktor ay ninanakaw ang pondo na dapat mapunta sa mga proyekto na makakatulong sa ating kalikasan at sa mga mahihirap, tulad na lamang ng maayos na drainage system at relokasyon sa ligtas na lugar.
Dahil dito, hindi lahat ng Pilipino ay may kakayahang bumangon o makaahon pagkatapos ng sakuna. Maraming nagugutom, nawawalan ng tirahan, at napipilitang mamuhay sa peligro. Bilang isang taong nakakaranas nito, alam ko gaano kahirap ang ganitong karanasan.
Kailangan natin ng pagbabago. Kailangan natin ng mga pinuno na tapat at may malasakit sa pinamumunuan niya. Sama-sama nating labanan ang korapsyon at ipaglaban ang karapatan nating mga PILIPINO.

Umabot na sa 9,108 ang kabuuang bilang ng aftershocks na naitala kasunod nang nangyaring Magnitude 6.9 Offshore Northern Cebu Earthquake noong Setyembre 30, 2025. 
1,666 sa mga ito ay plotted or located habang nasa 38 ang felt o naramdaman. Ang mga aftershocks ay mayroong magnitude range mula 1.0 hanggang 5.1. 
Ano ang 𝗔𝗙𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦𝗛𝗢𝗖𝗞𝗦?
Ito ay kasunod na mga pagyanig na kadalasang mas mahina kaysa sa naunang malakas at mapaminsalang lindol (main shock).
Ang ilan sa mga ito ay may sapat na lakas upang maramdaman. Ito ay maaaring maranasan ilang araw o kahit ilang linggo matapos ang mainshock.

Dalawang linggo matapos ang pananalasa ng Bagyong #OpongPH sa Bicol Region, patuloy ang Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) sa paghahatid ng tulong sa mga Bicolanong naapektuhan at ngayo’y unti-unti nang bumabangon mula sa pinsalang iniwan ng bagyo.
Bilang bahagi ng nagpapatuloy na pagtugon sa Masbate, muling lumipad si DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian sa island province para kumustahin ang kalagayan ng mga apektadong pamilya at alamin ang iba pang tulong na maaaring maiparating ng ahensya.
Sa pagbisita ng Kalihim sa Masbate, nakita niya ang pamamahagi ng DSWD Field Office 5 - Bicol Region ng 500 kahon ng family food packs (FFPs) sa mga residenteng apektado sa Dimasalang, Masbate ngayong Miyerkules (Oktubre 
.
Kasabay nito, nagpapatuloy din sa bayan ang medical mission ng DSWD katuwang ang Provincial Health Office ng Camarines Sur para matulungan ang mga residenteng nangangailangan ng agarang serbisyong medikal. Naka-deploy rin ang mobile kitchen para sa mainit na pagkain at water purifying truck na nagsisiguro sa ligtas at malinis na suplay ng inuming tubig para sa mga residente.
Kasama ni Secretary Gatchalian sa ikatlong biyahe sa Masbate sina Undersecretary Diana Rose Cajipe ng Disaster Response Management Group (DRMG, Field Office 5 Regional Director Norman Laurio, Dimasalang Mayor Michael Demph Naga, at Masbate Governor Ricardo Kho.

ICYMI: The 2nd day of GeoRiskPH for Resilience Regional Training, implemented by DOST-PHIVOLCS and the DRREALL-TA Project, continued to relay practical skills and knowledge on Disaster Risk Management to the participating local government units and learning resource institutes yesterday, October 8, 2025 at Richmonde Hotel, Eastwood City, Quezon City.
Ms. Gizella Marie Herrera, Project Coordinator of Agence Française de Développement (AFD) Philippines Country Office, delivered a message to the participants. Meanwhile, Dr. Marqueza L. Reyes of Expertise France lectured on Disaster Risk Management Framework and Aspects.
DOST-PHIVOLCS led a lecture on Earthquake and Volcanic Hazards while the Department of Environment and Natural Resources - Mines and Geosciences Bureau (DENR-MGB) discussed the Flooding and Landslide Hazards and DOST- Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) shared insights on Weather and Climate Hazards.
Also, DOST-PHIVOLCS taught the participants on the GeoRiskPh Platforms as well as utilizing these technologies to generate risk assessment and local planning processes which foster best practices in the implementation of GeoRiskPH.
Ms. Joan C. Salcedo of DOST-PHIVOLCS delivered the closing message, thanking the organizers and partner agencies in championing activities that demonstrate the progress and advancements made in GeoRiskPH and gather feedback from end-users and stakeholders.
