ICYMI: The 2nd day of GeoRiskPH for Resilience Regional Training, implemented by DOST-PHIVOLCS and the DRREALL-TA Project, continued to relay practical skills and knowledge on Disaster Risk Management to the participating local government units and learning resource institutes yesterday, October 8, 2025 at Richmonde Hotel, Eastwood City, Quezon City.
Dr. Marqueza L. Reyes of Expertise France lectured on Disaster Risk Management Framework and Aspects. Mr. John Harold B. Tabuzo of DOST-PHIVOLCS led a lecture on Earthquake and Volcanic Hazards while Dr. Karlo L. Queaño of DENR - Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) discussed the Flooding and Landslide Hazards and Ms. Mary May V. Calimoso of DOST- Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) shared insights on Weather and Climate Hazards.
Also, DOST-PHIVOLCS taught the participants on the GeoRiskPh Platform as well as utilizing these technologies to generate risk assessment and local planning processes which foster best practices in the implementation of GeoRiskPH.
Ms. Gizella Marie Herrera, Project Coordinator of Agence Française de Développement (AFD) Philippines Country Office delivered a message to the participants. Lastly, Ms. Joan C. Salcedo of DOST-PHIVOLCS thanked the organizers and partner agencies for championing activities that demonstrate the progress and advancements made in GeoRiskPH and gather feedback from end-users and stakeholders.

Tropical Storm NAKRI
Issued at 11:00 AM, 09 October 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next advisory at 11:00 PM today.
TROPICAL STORM “NAKRI” SLIGHTLY INTENSIFIES AS IT APPROACHES THE NORTHEASTERN BOUNDARY OF THE PHILIPPINE AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY.
Location of Center (10:00 AM):
The center of the Tropical Storm NAKRI was estimated based on all available data at 1,415 km East Northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon (OUTSIDE PAR) (23.3°N, 135.3°E). 
Intensity:
Maximum sustained winds of 75 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 90 km/h, and central pressure of 998 hPa. 
Present Movement:
North northwestward at 25 km/h 
Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds:
Strong to gale-force winds extend outwards up to 380 km from the center 
GENERAL OUTLOOK FOR THE FORECAST PERIOD
• NAKRI is forecast to move generally northwestward for the rest of the forecast period. It may enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) this afternoon or evening and will be given a local name “QUEDAN”.
• Inside PAR, QUEDAN will continue moving northwestward and may exit PAR tonight or tomorrow (10 October) early morning.
• This weather disturbance is forecast to continue intensifying while approaching Ryukyu Islands.
• NAKRI is less likely to directly affect the weather and sea conditions in the country throughout the forecast period. No Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal will be raised for this tropical cyclone. However, the southwesterlies and the northeasterly windflow will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):

   o Saturday (11 October): Ilocos Norte, Palawan, Romblon, Masbate, Western Visayas, Negros Island Region, Central Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, and Misamis Occidental
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to continue monitoring for updates related to this tropical cyclone. 
Unless there is an intermediate issuance, the next tropical cyclone advisory will be issued at 11:00 PM today.

Following the Magnitude 6.9 earthquake in Northern Cebu, the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) conducted a sinkhole inventory in the municipalities of San Remigio and Daanbantayan. These new sinkholes give us a rare glimpse into what lies beneath the ground surface.
Sinkholes, particularly those of the cover-collapse type, form when the ground surface suddenly collapses into underlying voids or cavities. This process can expose caves, which are often part of a larger, interconnected subsurface network. When a sinkhole forms above an aquifer containing water, it is referred to as a cenote, which exposes a deep depression filled with clear, turquoise blue water. The groundwater in these aquifers often resurfaces as karst springs, providing a vital source of water for local communities.

The City Engineer’s Office, in coordination with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), has completed structural assessments of Bankerohan Bridge, Bolton Bridge, Davao River Bridge, and San Rafael Bridge. We urge the public to remain calm and vigilant. Please continue to monitor official channels for accurate and timely updates regarding the situation and potential aftershocks.

Davao City Earthquake Update
As of 3:30 PM, October 10, 2025
As of 3:30 PM today, unfortunately, there is one (1) confirmed fatality related to the earthquake incident in Davao City. The City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) has already reached out to the victim’s family to provide the necessary assistance.
The City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO)-Central 911 have swiftly responded to a total of 347 individuals who experienced fainting or sustained minor injuries. All patients have received proper medical attention and are now in stable condition.
Following the issuance of a Red Alert Status by the Office of Civil Defense for the Davao Region, the Davao City DRRMO has likewise raised its alert status to Red Alert. All emergency assets are currently prepositioned in preparation for possible aftershocks.
There is no active tsunami warning for Davao City.
The City Engineer’s Office, in coordination with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), has completed structural assessments of Bankerohan Bridge, Bolton Bridge, Davao River Bridge, and San Rafael Bridge. No major structural damage was found. All four bridges are declared safe for vehicular traffic.
We urge the public to remain calm and vigilant. Please continue to monitor official channels for accurate and timely updates regarding the situation and potential aftershocks.

Davao de Oro has already received P1.17 million worth of assistance from the Department of Social Welfare and Development-Davao Region (DSWD-Davao) following the recent strong earthquakes that jolted parts of Mindanao.
Based on data from the Regional Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council-Davao  (RDRRMC-Davao) the tremors affected 4 municipalities and 28 barangays, displacing 699 families or 3,070 individuals.
Of these, 224 families or 849 individuals are temporarily sheltered in evacuation centers. The earthquake also damaged 361 houses, with 9 totally destroyed and 352 partially damaged.
The DSWD reported that the assistance included 2,000 family food packs distributed to affected communities as part of its ongoing emergency response operations.

October 12, 2025
Office of Civil Defense (OCD) Administrator, Undersecretary Harold Cabreros, led an aerial and ground assessment in the Davao Region on Saturday following the "doublet earthquake"—two main shocks that struck Davao Oriental on Friday morning and evening.
Usec. Cabreros arrived in Davao City late Friday evening and immediately met with OCD Davao Regional Director Ednar Dayanghirang and Operations Center staff to discuss the situation. Follow-up briefings were conducted on Saturday morning with the OCD Davao Region and the Tactical Operations Group Davao to finalize plans for the aerial survey and ocular inspections.
The assessment team included representatives from the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB), the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS), OCD Davao Director Dayanghirang, and officers from uniformed services. Aside from aerial survey, their activities included a meeting with Davao Oriental Governor Nelson Dayanghirang in Mati; inspection of several damaged facilities in Manay, Davao Oriental, including a community hospital and a barangay hall; and a coordination meeting in Pantukan, Davao de Oro, with Governor Raul Mabanglo and local officials to address landslides and ongoing threats in the municipality.
Following the assessment, Usec. Cabreros reported online to an inter-agency meeting of NDRRMC, confirming the priority areas based on the severity of damage in Davao:
Manay, Davao Oriental
Tarragona, Davao Oriental
Mati City, Davao Oriental
Pantukan, Davao de Oro
“We did an air survey of affected areas and ocular inspections of the ground. We have validated initial damages, based on our collaboration with LGUs and governors of Davao de Oro, Davao Oriental, the Mayor of Manay, and the Mayor of Pantukan. Manay is the priority, then Tarragona, Mati, and finally Pantukan, in that order.” he stated.
Usec. Cabreros highlighted the vulnerability of health infrastructure, noting that the health sector was the "most affected." The Davao Oriental Provincial Hospital in Manay is currently non-operational due to heavy and structurally unstable damage. Concerned agencies are coordinating structural and functional assessments of all damaged health facilities to prioritize repair needs and identify safe alternative patient accommodation to ensure operational continuity.
PHIVOLCS recorded two main tremors in Manay, Davao Oriental, on Friday: a Magnitude 7.4 earthquake at 9:43 A.M., followed by a Magnitude 6.8 shock at 7:12 P.M. Tsunami warnings were issued, prompting forced evacuations led by Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) Offices, the Philippine National Police (PNP), the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), and the Department of Tourism (DOT). These warnings were subsequently lifted. The highest reported intensity in Manay was Intensity VI.
Basic needs, including food and water, are reported as sufficient in affected areas, with temporary shelters provided by respective local government units. The national government has assured its readiness to augment resources as needed.
OCD Davao Region and other affected regions are continuously conducting assessments and coordinating with local DRRM Councils. 
Various government agencies and uniformed services have been holding a series of coordination meetings since Friday to monitor the situation and coordinate assistance on the ground.

DISASTER RESPONSE UPDATE | Temporary Modular Housing, Bagong Simula Para sa mga Taga San Remigio, Cebu
Bagong tahanan na pupunuin ng mga bagong alaala ang kasalukuyang itinatayo sa San Remigio, Cebu. Katuwang ang Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), pinangunahan ng Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) ang pagtatayo ng mga modular housing units sa tinatawag na Bayanihan Village.
Sa ngayon, 21 units na ang naitayo, kabilang ang 8 na hinihintay na lang malagyan ng kuryente. Naihatid na rin karagdagang 40 units. Target na matapos maitayo ng DHSUD ang mahigit 60 modular housing units sa susunod na linggo.
Kapag handa na ang Bayanihan Village, saka papasok ang DSWD para sa camp management katuwang ang LGU ng San Remigio. Prayoridad dito ang mga pamilyang nawalan ng tahanan dahil sa lindol, habang ang mga matitirang mga units ay para sa mga nasa no-build zones.
Kasama ito sa pagtupad ni Secretary Rex Gatchalian sa direktiba ni Pangulong Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. na mabigyan ng maayos na matutuluyan ang mga pamilyang apektado ng sakuna na siya ring nagpapatunay ng sama-samang malasakit ng iba’t ibang national agencies.

[ RD IN ACTION ] DAY 2 | RD Conducts Site Assessment and Monitoring in Quake-Hit Areas of Davao Oriental 
Earlier today, FCSUPT JUNITO F MASLANG, Regional Director of the Bureau of Fire Protection Region 11, together with FSUPT JOYCELYN HERNAEZ-GRANT, Provincial Fire Marshal, FCINSP PAUL JORGE C BARROZO, and FSINSP ELIZABETH D CAPIÑA, personally visited the municipalities of Manay and Tarragona in Davao Oriental to assess the impact of the magnitude 7.6 earthquake that recently struck the province.
The team conducted thorough inspection and monitoring activities at critical areas, including Manay Fire Station, Davao Oriental Provincial Hospital, Tarragona Municipal Hall, and Tarragona Fire Station, to evaluate structural integrity and ensure operational readiness of BFP units.
During the visit, FCSUPT MASLANG met with key officials of both municipalities to coordinate efforts and reinforce the Bureau’s support in the ongoing response and recovery operations. He emphasized the importance of close collaboration between the BFP and the Local Government Units (LGUs) to ensure the safety of affected residents and the swift restoration of essential services.
The Regional Director likewise commended the dedication of BFP personnel on the ground, urging them to remain vigilant and proactive in assisting local authorities in disaster response and community safety operations. NILIPAD 'YUNG MGA LOBO 
Uploader Filipina Maloto shared a video showing a bunch of balloons for sale accidentally floating away.
She looked for “Nanay,” the vendor often seen in front of the church in Concepcion, Marikina, bought some of her remaining balloons, and paid P1,000 to help out.
Nanay explained that she accidentally let go of the balloons while assisting a customer. “Bayaran pa naman ng bahay. Maiyak-iyak na ko talaga, pero nilalakasan ko lang ‘yung loob ko,” she said.
“Ang sabi ko po, sa kaniya na ‘yung sukli. Tapos ayun, sobrang saya ni Nanay napaiyak na kami parehas kasi ‘di siya makapaniwala,” the uploader recalled.
Meanwhile, the story touched many, inspiring donations of cash and groceries for Nanay.

The other LPA was located 1,780 km east of northeastern Mindanao, outside the PAR.
It has medium potential for tropical cyclone formation in the next 24 hours.
This disturbance may enter the PAR as a tropical cyclone on Friday and will be named #RamilPH.
It may head towards Northern Luzon this weekend or Taiwan early next week.

 Step 1: Open Settings
Go to your phone’s 
 Settings app.
 Step 2: Find Safety & Emergency (or Location)
On most phones: Settings → Safety & emergency
On some brands (Samsung, Xiaomi, etc.): it might be under Settings → Location → Earthquake alerts.
 Step 3: Enable Earthquake Alerts
Look for Earthquake alerts.
Toggle ON to allow your phone to use Google’s Android Earthquake Alerts System.
 Step 4: Test
You won’t get a “test alert” option (unlike emergency alerts), but once enabled, your phone will vibrate and show a push notification if a significant quake is detected nearby.
---
 Tips:
Keep location and internet/data on — the system relies on both.

TURN ON YOUR EARTHQUAKE ALERTS ON YOUR PHONES. Seconds Can Save Lives 
During the recent earthquakes in Cebu, many Android users were able to move to safety just in time, thanks to the Earthquake Alert System on their phones. This powerful feature uses signals from nearby seismic activity and Google’s network of sensors to give you a few precious seconds’ warning before the shaking starts. Those seconds can mean the difference between safety and danger.
 Make sure YOUR Android phone is ready and your Location is turned on:
Samsung, Xiaomi, Redmi, Poco, Oppo, Vivo, Realme, Huawei (for models with Android/Google services), Tecno, Infinix, Motorola, Nokia (Android models), and OnePlus.
How to Turn On Earthquake Alerts (Android):
 Open Settings on your Android phone.
 Tap Safety & Emergency (on some devices, look under Location or Security & Emergency).
 Select Earthquake Alerts.
 Toggle ON to enable alerts.
 Once activated, your phone will automatically warn you if an earthquake is detected in your area.
Let’s all stay one step ahead—prepare, pray, stay alert, and stay safe.

“Ang Di‐Inaasahang Lindol sa Mindanao Kaninang Umaga”
Kanina lang umaga, isang malakas na lindol na may tinatayang magnitude 7.4 (o mas mataas pa sa ilang pagtataya) ang yumanig sa rehiyon ng Mindanao, lalong-lalo na sa baybayin ng Davao Oriental malapit sa bayan ng Manay. 
 Nagdulot ito ng pagyanig sa lupa sa maraming lugar, pagbagsak o pagbitak ng mga pader at gusali, pagkasira sa ospital, at pagka‐evacuate sa mga pasyente. 
 Mga coastal areas ay nilisan pansamantala dahil sa banta ng tsunami, bagaman kalaunan ay binawi ang tsunami alert. 
The Guardian
 Sa ngayon, kumpirmado nang may dalawang patay sa Davao Oriental dahil sa pagbagsak ng gusali. 
 Mysterious / Teoretikal na Pagsusuri
Pag‐galaw sa Philippine Trench
May teorya na ang lindol ay nagmula sa paggalaw ng isang segment sa Philippine Trench, isang lugar kung saan nagtatagpo ang mga tectonic plates sa ilalim ng dagat. 
 Ang ganitong pag‐galaw ay maaaring magtulak ng seabed pataas o pababa—na siya namang puwedeng magpagalaw ng tubig sa ibabaw, na nagiging sanhi ng tsunami. 
Submarine Landslides
Isang posibilidad ay may pagguho sa ilalim ng dagat (submarine landslide) na nangyari dahil sa malakas na get-o galaw ng lupa sa ilalim ng dagat. Ang ganitong pagguho ay puwedeng maglatag ng dagdag na gibain sa pagtaas o pagbaba ng tubig sa baybayin. Ito’y mas subtle at mahirap mapansin agad.
Aftershocks / Chain Reaction
Dahil dati’y nagkaroon ng malalakas na lindol sa iba’t ibang bahagi ng Pilipinas nitong mga nakaraang araw (halimbawa sa Cebu) 
, may posibilidad na ang stress sa mga fault lines ay nag‐accumulate. Kapag may lindol sa isang bahagi, maaaring magkaroon ito ng domino effect sa katabing faults.
Fault Complexity / Hidden Faults
Posible ring may hindi pa natutuklasang pinagsisikipan o fault line sa ilalim ng dagat o sa karatig na lupain. Sa ilang malalakas na lindol sa kasaysayan, lumitaw na may bahagi ng fault na hindi pa nakikita o hindi pa nailalarawan ng mga geologists.
Anomalous Phenomena / Sigaw ng Kalikasan
Sa aspetong “misteryoso,” may mga naniniwala rin sa mga sinaunang paniniwala—na ang lindol ay senyales mula sa kalikasan, o reaksyon sa masyadong labis na pagsamantala sa lupa, deforestation, pagmimina, o pagbabago sa ilalim ng dagat. Hindi ito sang‐ayon sa agham, ngunit madalas lumalabas sa mga lokal na kuwento at teoryang popular paminsan-minsan.
 Disclaimer (Para sa Edukasyunal na Layunin Lamang)
Ang nilalaman dito ay teoretikal at circumstantial lamang—hindi ito opisyal na ulat mula sa Phivolcs o iba pang mapagkakatiwalaang ahensya. Huwag ituring ito bilang huling hatol o totoong paliwanag. Para sa mas tamang impormasyon, mangyaring sumangguni sa Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) o lokal na awtoridad sa agham at kalikasang sakuna.

Mandato ni Pangulong Bong Bong Marcos Jr., na maagang maghanda sa mga sakuna at siguruhing hindi maaantala ang mga serbisyo ng iba’t ibang ahensya. 
Kinumpirma ni DOH Sec. Ted Herbosa na nakahanda ang Department of Health (DOH) sakaling tumama ang “The Big One”, o ang 7.2 magnitude na lindol sa Metro Manila.
Sa DOH contingency plan, hinati ang Metro Manila sa apat na quadrant at nagtalaga ng DOH hospital sa bawat quadrant para maging maayos at mabilis ang pagresponde sakaling mangyari ang malakas na lindol.
Pasado sa Hospital Safety Index ang mga istruktura ng DOH Hospitals at nakalatag na ang mga emergency contingency plan para sa 7.2 magnitude na lindol. 
Ilan sa mga regular na hakbang na siniguro ng DOH sa mga ospital nito ay ang assessment ng structural
integrity ng mga buildings at pasilidad gamit ang mga pag-aaral ng DOH at partners nito, at Hospital safety Index tool. Ilang structural retrofitting na rin ang nagawa sa ilang pasilidad na matagal nang nakatayo. 
Mahalagang alam ng publiko ang mapa ng mga DOH hospitals para sa North, East, West, at South quadrants. Kaagapay din ng DOH NCR ang mga kalapit na rehiyon, gaya ng REGION III, at agad na reresponde sakaling tumama sa Metro Manila ang malakas na lindol.

Ilan sa mga regular na hakbang na siniguro ng DOH sa mga ospital nito ay ang assessment ng structural integrity ng mga buildings at pasilidad gamit ang mga pag-aaral ng DOH at partners nito, at Hospital safety Index tool. Ilang structural retrofitting na rin ang nagawa sa ilang pasilidad na matagal nang nakatayo. Mahalagang alam ng publiko ang mapa ng mga DOH hospitals para sa North, East, West, at South quadrants. Hindi pwede iprograma sa NCAP system na lahat ng may blinkers at sirens ay automatic na exempt sa huli dahil baka may manamantala nito. 
Kailangan din siguraduhin na lehitimo na emergency vehicle talaga ang sasakyan dahil meron nang insidente noon na isang service ng funeraria ay nilagyan ng tatak na ambulance. 
Malinaw din ang naging pahayag ng MMDA na kapag hindi reresponde sa emergency ay hindi dapat lumabag sa batas trapiko ang mga emergency vehicles.

VISITS DAVAO ORIENTAL; BFP 11 CONDUCTS BRIEFING AND GROUND COORDINATION IN TARRAGONA FS |  Under the leadership of FCSUPT JUNITO F MASLANG, DSC, Regional Director of the Bureau of Fire Protection Region 11, BFP personnel conducted a thorough briefing at Tarragona Fire Station as part of the ongoing response and coordination efforts in the province. 
Following the briefing, the team proceeded to the designated landing zone to meet President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., who was visiting the area to personally check the situation of affected communities. The BFP team also conducted coordination and monitoring in key locations, including the Davao Oriental Provincial Hospital, Manay National High School, and the Tarragona Evacuation Center, to assess the conditions and ensure public safety.
During his visit, President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. personally checked on the welfare of hospital staff and patients at Davao Oriental Provincial Hospital–Manay. He was joined by members of his Cabinet and officials of the local government of Davao Oriental, reaffirming the national government’s commitment to support disaster response and recovery in the province.
The joint efforts of the national government and BFP Region 11, under the guidance of FCSUPT MASLANG, highlight a unified commitment to public safety, disaster preparedness, and effective emergency response for the people of Davao Oriental. When oarfish come up to the surface or wash ashore, it usually means something unusual is happening in the ocean — but not necessarily that an earthquake is coming (a common myth). Here are the real scientific reasons why oarfish might come out: 1. They’re sick, injured, or dying. Oarfish normally live deep in the ocean (about 200–1,000 meters below). If they’re old, injured, or sick, they lose strength and float up to the surface. 2. Changes in water temperature or pressure. Sudden shifts — like warmer water from climate changes, or underwater volcanic activity — can force them to move closer to the surface. 3. Strong currents or storms. Typhoons, underwater landslides, or strong ocean currents can push deep-sea creatures like oarfish toward shallow waters or beaches. 4. Lack of oxygen in deep waters. If oxygen levels drop in their natural habitat (due to pollution or algae blooms), they rise to find better conditions. 5. Earthquake myth — half-true. In Japanese folklore, oarfish are called “messengers from the sea god’s palace” and believed to warn of earthquakes or tsunamis. However, scientists have no proven evidence linking oarfish sightings directly to earthquakes. They might just be reacting to small underwater disturbances — not predicting quakes.

On this International Day of Rural Women, we honor the strength and indispensable role of women who feed nations, nurture communities, and sustain livelihoods from the grassroots—while confronting the roots of their own struggles.
Bound by systems that place profit over people, indigenous and peasant women remain shackled by the chains of exploitation and exclusion so long as land remains monopolized in the hands of the elite and corporate interests. They also continue to face limited access to education, inadequate healthcare, and pervasive gender-based violence and discrimination.
Implementing genuine agrarian reform and gender-responsive rural development policies are crucial to ensure that they may reap their fruits with dignity, equality, and ownership. 
To liberate women is to emancipate our people from the semi-feudal conditions—the oppressive grip of profit-driven landlords, corporations, and a system that functions beyond the control of those who till the land.

“If we do have 'The Big One,' most of the casualties will come from the ISFs, because they use — none of their buildings are constructed with the municipal permits, and they cook with kerosine and with other non-regulated cooking implements, and that is the major cause of fires, and that will be the major cause of damage,” sabi ni Remulla.
Samantala, magkakaroon ng infrastructure audit na magsisimula sa National Capital Region, Calabarzon, at Central Luzon, ayon kay DILG Undersecretary Marlo Iringan.

Various Filipino women's groups and progressives demand "food for people, not profit" during two protest actions in front of the Department of Agriculture (DA) in Quezon City on October 15, 2025.
National federation of peasant women Amihan said their protest "symbolizes the collective fight of the Filipino rural and peasant women "against Marcos systemic-wide corruption."
The Asian Peoples' Movement on Debt and Development
(APMDD) and Oriang-led protest in the country is part of Asia-wide actions on Rural Women’s Day, joining other women in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
"Asia is a chronically food-insecure and climate-vulnerable region, and food insecurity affects more women than men everywhere in the world. This year in the Philippines, agricultural losses from Tropical Cyclones Crising, Dante, and Emong amounted to P2.34 billion, depleting the country’s food supply and raising food prices. Over 75,000 farmers and 72,000 hectares of farmland were affected, with the rice sector accounting for half the losses," APMDD said in a statement. I Photos by Guia Mistades and Jimmy A. WHERE IS THE PRESIDENT NOW?
While Typhoon Crising lashes the Philippines, leaving entire towns flooded, homes destroyed, and Filipinos crying for help, our President is abroad—comfortably meeting with the US President.
 This is leadership?
In the face of calamity, when his people need him the most, he chooses to leave. No direct presence, no leadership on the ground. Just silence. Is this the kind of leader we deserve?
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, the President is the Commander-in-Chief and must be present and accountable in times of national emergency. Leaving the country without declaring who is in command violates his constitutional duties.
 LEGAL BASIS: 
 Article VII, Section 4 – The President shall ensure the faithful execution of the laws and must uphold accountability to the people.
 Article XI, Section 1 – Public officers, including the President, must at all times be accountable to the people.
 Article XI, Section 2 – The President may be removed from office on impeachment for culpable violation of the Constitution, betrayal of public trust, or gross neglect of duty.
 Abandoning the nation during a declared State of Calamity without properly delegating emergency authority can be considered gross negligence and betrayal of public trust.
Is this the kind of leader we want — one who leaves during disaster? Or do we deserve someone who will stand and lead in the storm?
 Is this the kind of leader we deserve?

Senator Bam Aquino's Philippine National Budget Blockchain Bill captured public attention, especially given the timing around flood-control controversies. The current outrage has ignited an important conversation on how public funds are spent-- and potentially hidden. In the uproar over stalled projects and missing allocations, the bill promised a clean fix: put every peso on the blockchain. Each transaction, it claimed, would live forever on an immutable ledger—visible to all, tamper-proof, and honest by design. It’s a seductive vision: that technology could finally do what politics hasn’t.
But that’s the problem. We keep mistaking technology for reform. Blockchain is treated as the cure, not the tool. As if corruption were a software bug, not a symptom of power, discretion, and inequality. The assumption is that when code is incorruptible, people will become so too. Yet history reminds us that tools inherit their makers’ hands—and their habits.

Lumakas pa bilang Tropical Storm ang bagyong #RamilPH na may int’l name na ngayong #FENGSHEN habang patuloy na tinutumbok ang probinsya ng #Catanduanes sa #BicolRegion.

Bukas mas mararamdaman ang masungit na lagay ng panahon sa malaking bahagi ng #Luzon dahil sa inaasahang pagtawid ng bagyo sa kalupaan.
Patuloy na pinag-iingat ang ating mga kababayan na maaapektuhan ng bagyo sa banta ng mga biglaang pagbaha at mga pagguho ng lupa na kaakibat ng mga pag-ulan na dala ng bagyo.

Severe Winds
The wind signals warn the public of the general wind threat over an area due to the tropical cyclone. Local winds may be slightly stronger/enhanced in coastal and upland/mountainous areas exposed to winds. Winds are less strong in areas sheltered from the prevailing wind direction.
• Minor to moderate impacts from gale-force winds are possible within any of the localities where Wind Signal No. 2 is hoisted
• Minimal to minor impacts from strong winds are possible within any of the areas under Wind Signal No. 1.

TROPICAL STORM RAMIL MAKES LANDFALL IN SORSOGON; HEAVY RAINS THREATEN LUZON AND VISAYAS
Tropical Storm Ramil (international name: Fengshen) has officially made landfall in southeastern Luzon, near Sorsogon and the Bicol Region, after tracking slightly farther south and west than early forecasts predicted.
Now moving slowly westward, Ramil is expected to cross the Bicol Region before heading toward Southern and Central Luzon, including areas near Metro Manila and Pangasinan, throughout the weekend.
PAGASA has raised Signal No. 2 over parts of Northern Samar and the eastern coast. However, the main concern is heavy rainfall, not wind — with 100 to 200 mm expected along the east coast and 50 to 150 mm across Bicol, Samar, and eventually much of Luzon.
Residents are warned of localized flooding and landslides, especially in mountainous and low-lying areas. Even regions north of the storm’s center may experience widespread rain due to its broad convection.
Authorities urge the public to stay alert and not focus solely on the storm’s center track, as outer rainbands often cause the most significant impacts.

𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: The key difference between a 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 and a 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲 lies in their forecast period, coverage areas, and accuracy. A 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 provides forecasts for the next three hours and applies up to the municipal level. It is more precise as it utilizes Doppler radar technology to track real-time rainfall intensity, making it highly effective for immediate decision-making in flood-prone areas. A 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲, on the other hand, covers a 24-hour period but is issued only at the provincial level. It provides a broader outlook on potential weather disturbances but lacks the short-term accuracy of 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬. For class suspensions or other official decisions, please refer to 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐲 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 issued by the respective PAGASA Regional Services Divisions.

Nais ituwid ng Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) ang lumabas na news article ng ABS-CBN kung saan nakasaad na hindi exempted ang mga emergency vehicle sa No Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP).
Sa panayam kay MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes ng isang ABS-CBN reporter, malinaw niyang sinabi na hindi awtomatikong exempted sa mga traffic violations ang mga emergency vehicle. Hindi lahat ng may blinkers at sirena ay exempted sa batas-trapiko. Isa ito sa dahilan kung bakit hindi pwede automatic ang exemption. 
Kinakailangang masiguro na lehitimong emergency vehicle ang sasakyan. Hindi dapat iprograma sa NCAP system na lahat ng may blinkers at siren ay automatic na exempt sa huli dahil maaring may manamantala nito. 
Nagkaroon na ng insidente kung saan ang isang funeral vehicle ay nagpanggap na "ambulance" para makadaan sa EDSA Busway. Nahuli ito ng Special Action and Intelligence Committee for Transportation (SAICT).
Sa ilalim ng NCAP, ang mga mahuhuli ng AI-technology CCTV cameras ay sasailalim sa automatic review. Ibig sabihin, mano-mano itong rerebyuhin ng aming NCAP personnel. Kapag napatunayang mali ang pagkakahuli, i-invalidate ito at hindi makatatanggap ng notice of violation.
Kung walang emergency, hindi dapat lumalabag sa mga traffic rules ang mga emergency vehicle.
Umaasa ang MMDA na sa tulong ng mga media entities, maihahatid ang impormasyon sa publiko nang tama at beripikado.
